title: Prime-factor induction
statement:
If a statement about torsion sheaves is stable under short exact sequences,
then its verification for all $F[n]$ reduces by induction on the total number
of prime factors of $n$ to its verification for sheaves killed by one prime.

proof.text:
Choose a prime $\ell\mid n$ and use the short exact sequence
$0\to F[\ell]\to F[n]\xrightarrow{\ell}\ell F[n]\to0$.
The kernel is killed by $\ell$, while $\ell F[n]$ is killed by $n/\ell$ and
therefore has fewer prime factors in its exponent. Let
$C(F)=\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F})$ and use the
cohomological cone convention
$d_{C}(y,x)=(d_Yy+u(x),-d_Xx)$. Applying the two derived functors to the
short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle of exchange maps and,
by the octahedral axiom, a triangle

$$
C(F[\ell])\longrightarrow C(F[n])\longrightarrow
C(\ell F[n])\xrightarrow{+1}C(F[\ell])[1].
$$

The connecting map is the class of $(y,x)\mapsto y$ in the above cone
convention; the sign in the last arrow is forced by
$d_C^2=0$. Induct on
$\nu(n)=\sum_\ell v_\ell(n)$. If the two end cones are acyclic, the long
exact cohomology sequence of this triangle makes the middle cone acyclic.
The base $\nu(n)=1$ is the prime-torsion input. This displays the invariant
and all connecting morphisms.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\square$ a cartesian square, and let
$\Ex^q_{\square,E}:g^{-1}R^qf_*E\to R^qf'_*g'^{-1}E$ be the degree-$q$ exchange
maps of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] on sheaves $E$ of $\Lambda$-modules on
$X_{\Et}$. Suppose that $\Ex^q_{\square,E}$ is an isomorphism for every $q$ and
every sheaf $E$ killed by a prime. Then $\Ex^q_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism
for every $q$ and every sheaf $F$ killed by a positive integer $n$.

proof.text:
Let $P(E)$ be the property that $\Ex^q_{\square,E}$ is an isomorphism for every
$q$. By the five-lemma transfer [lemma-weil-pbc-five-lemma-transfer], $P$ is
stable under extensions: if $0\to F_1\to F\to F_2\to0$ is exact and $P$ holds
for $F_1$ and $F_2$, it holds for $F$. By hypothesis $P$ holds for every sheaf
killed by a prime. The prime-factor devissage
[lem-weil-pbc-prime-factor-devissage] in the abelian category of sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ then gives $P(F)$ for every $F$ killed by a
positive integer $n$. Explicitly, one inducts on the number of prime factors of
$n$: for $n=1$ the sheaf $F=0$ is killed by any prime, and otherwise, for a
prime $\ell\mid n$, the sequence $0\to F[\ell]\to F\xrightarrow{\ell}\ell F\to0$
has kernel killed by $\ell$ and image killed by $n/\ell$, so $P$ holds for both
ends and hence for $F$.
